title: Greenland
capsule: Greenland, the world's largest island, was colonized by Norse settlers under Erik the Red from c. 985 CE and converted to Christianity under Leif Erikson around 1000, but these settlements died out by the fifteenth century. Danish crown authority was re-established after 1721 when Hans Egede founded a mission colony at Godthab (Nuuk), making Greenland a royal colony integrated into the Danish-Norwegian realm; following the dissolution of Denmark-Norway in 1814, Greenland passed entirely to Denmark. The island's colonial status was formalized in the nineteenth century, with Denmark exercising monopoly trade through the Royal Greenland Trading Department (KGH, founded 1776); the dataset attests this colonial period from 1734 to 1940, which ends with the German occupation of Denmark in April 1940 disrupting normal administration.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The geographic extent of Greenland as a physical island is precisely known; the effective area of Danish colonial administration was confined to scattered coastal settlements, and the interior ice sheet was essentially uncontrolled — dataset geometry likely represents the island's full outline rather than administered area.
